integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot1] An original expressive stylized3D animated Brazilian street-news comedy at a peaceful gamers protest. Fictional ADULT humans only, rounded appealing faces, matte colorful clothes, grounded feet, coherent five-finger hands, independent acting. Not live action and no real person imitation. Warm afternoon light from screen-left, soft shadows. A fictional unbranded red-brick electronics storefront on one Brazilian square. No weapons, violence, fire, smoke, logos, price tags, news graphics, subtitles, watermarks or music.
Vertical768x1344. One uninterrupted eye-level medium-wide interview, reporter screen-left and interviewee screen-right, large readable faces and clear hands. A small slow physical dolly to camera-right changes perspective: nearby wooden sign poles shift relative to the speakers and the distant brick doorway. Three real depth layers, stable axis, no zoom, orbit, spin, cuts or shake. Speakers stay planted, with natural weight shifts. Clothing follows their separate gestures.
EXACTLY TWO very large rectangular pale warm-ivory BLANK protest placards face camera in the upper part of the portrait frame. One board at upper-left and one upper-right; each wide landscape rectangle approximately320pixels wide and230pixels high. All four corners and the COMPLETE paper surfaces remain visible with at least24pixels outer margin. Their lower edges stay above every person's hair with a visible gap. Two adults behind the interview hold only the wooden sticks below the boards. Never wave a board across a face. Slow tiny independent board sway, neither sign leaves the frame. NO other signs. Both surfaces are completely BLANK with no drawn image, generated letter, number, logo, symbol or pseudowriting; LARGE EXACT typography will be added later as deterministic graphics. Keep all of both clean paper interiors clear throughout the shot.
Only the indicated adult speaks at each moment. Intelligible natural Brazilian Portuguese, normal cadence, original fictional adult voices. Listen with mouth closed, look toward the current speaker. No added words, overlapping dialogue or anticipatory laughter. Crowd stays quiet under speech and reacts only after the punchline. Physical action and independent eye/hand/cloth motion continue through the final frame, with a deliberate recovery rather than repeating gestures or holding a frozen pose.
FIRST independent interview. Reporter: fictional Brazilian adult woman in her30s, chestnut straight bob haircut, plain navy-blue jacket over a cream shirt and dark jeans. Her right hand holds ONE plain black microphone. Gamer: fictional Brazilian adult man in his40s with tan skin, short black hair with one silver streak, small trimmed dark beard, plain olive-green button-up shirt and dark jeans. He holds ONE old generic graphics card horizontally against his lower chest with BOTH hands. The GPU is a single chunky rectangular dark cooler with ONE round fan and metal fins, no branding or writing. Its size, fan count and shape stay constant. He supports the cooler body without covering his face. No computer tower, smartphone, keys, money, paper or extra object.
His objective is to protect and defend the sentimental family GPU. The joke is that even his son will inherit this obsolete board instead of getting an upgrade. Nobody sells or drops it, no offscreen child appears.
0.0-3.6s: Reporter looks briefly toward the old GPU, then meets his eyes and asks exactly <d>[Portuguese] Quando você vai trocar essa placa?</d>. Gamer listens with closed mouth, holding his GPU protectively. She moves the microphone toward him after finishing the question.
3.6-6.6s: Gamer looks down fondly at the GPU and begins his one answer exactly <d>[Portuguese] Ela foi do meu pai…</d>. His elbows relax a little, showing the fan and fins without twisting the card. Reporter listens seriously.
6.6-7.2s: A short natural comic pause. He looks back toward the reporter, still cradling the SAME card. Crowd remains quiet.
7.2-10.3s: Gamer finishes his answer in dry resignation, exactly <d>[Portuguese] agora meu filho que lute!</d>. Stress filho que lute with a small knowing half-smile. Both hands continue supporting the one GPU. No second sentence.
10.3-12.5s: Reporter looks from his face to the old card, realizes the inheritance joke, then gives ONE brief amused laugh. Crowd responds with one short late laugh. He lifts the SAME GPU only a few centimeters toward her, presenting his precious family heirloom, without handing it over.
12.5-15.083s: Gamer safely brings the GPU back against his torso. Reporter turns her free left palm toward the two BLANK protest boards while retaining the microphone in her right hand. He follows her gaze, makes one resigned nod, and the crowd settles into a small grounded recovery with gentle board sway. No extra dialogue, chant, looping laugh or frozen final pose.
overall_soundscape: Clear original female question and warm slightly gravelly adult male reply in Brazilian Portuguese. Short natural pause between pai and agora, one brief shared laugh AFTER lute. Subdued street ambience and faint cardboard rustle; no music, no extra words, no real-person voice imitation.
non_diegetic_music: None.
